_about: Census-people basis store for the 1996 federal election (the 1996-census side of the people-interp lane for that frame — derive-booth-demo-90s.py's six-store output; see its header). The people-smallest-area is a 1996-census collection district: a booth's demo block is that CD's census counts pinned to the venue's approximate location from data/booth-locations-history.json (the map's own published history-venue store; pre-2001 elections have no AEC coordinate roll), a division's the exact census sum over the CDs whole-allocated to the era's division set (seifa-src/cd-1996-ced-1996set.json — the Parliamentary Handbook era polygons, the map's published era set). Venue-to-CD mapping is point-in-poly where the venue point sits inside a district, and the era-nearest CD along the era's own survey-draft linework within 1,500 m (counts.boothsGeoNearest, those venues' median rescue distance counts.geoNearestDistP50, p95 counts.geoNearestDistP95) where no district contains it — the era boundaries' drafting vintage puts most venue points within a couple of hundred metres of the printed line. The '90s lane is the six GCP-era lanes measured on the census's own AURIN Basic Community Profile lane (extract-bcp-aurin-tally.py): persons, ages, home-language share, birthplace, education level, blue-collar occupation. COB country menu, religion, tenure, year-12, Indigenous status and one-parent keys ride the 2001-and-later arcs' own census editions only — the '90s stores carry none of those keys by design. The census's ABS-filed balance classes named offshoreClass in the allocation file are dropped here entirely by ABS's own filing.
deliveryBasis: venue PIP of the history-location-store coordinates over the 1996-census CD polygons; exact CD sum per division (seifa-src/cd-1996-ced-1996set.json)
